headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin Test
summary: The Tigers secure a landmark victory on Australian soil, ending a 23-year wait for a Test win away from home against the Kangaroos.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in the opening Test in Darwin, with Australia captain Pat Cummins admitted that the visitors outplayed them in all facets of the game.

After bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings, Bangladesh piled up 426 runs, securing a commanding 228-run lead. Despite Cameron Green's 104 in the second innings, Australia were bowled out for 284.

Chasing a small target of 57 runs, Bangladesh reached the goal with the loss of only one wicket. Shadman Islam (25*) and Mominul Haque (30*) remained unbeaten to seal the victory in the second session of the fourth day.
The win marks a historic milestone for Bangladesh cricket, ending a 23-year wait for a Test victory on Australian soil since the Cardiff match in 2003.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, praising the team's performance and specifically mentioning Tanzid Hasan Tamim's contribution.

Former Australian cricketer Mark Waugh own the win as the 'biggest upset I can remember in Australia', while Pat Cummins admitted there was no excuse for the hosts' failure to penetrate with the ball.
The two teams will face off again in the second Test scheduled to begin in Mackay on August 22.
caption:
A 23-year wait is over! Bangladesh just secured a historic 9-wicket victory over Australia on their own soil.

Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in the opening Test in Darwin, with Australia captain Pat Cummins admitted that the visitors outplayed them in all facets of the game.

After bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings, Bangladesh piled up 426 runs, securing a commanding 228-run lead. Despite Cameron Green's 104 in the second innings, Australia were bowled out for 284.

Chasing a small target of 57 runs, Bangladesh reached the goal with the loss of only one wicket. Shadman Islam (25*) and Mominul Haque (30*) remained unbeaten to seal the victory in the second session of the fourth day.

The win marks a historic milestone for Bangladesh cricket, ending a 23-year wait for a Test victory on Australian soil since the Cardiff match in 2003.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, praising the team's performance and specifically mentioning Tanzid Hasan Tamim's contribution.

Former Australian cricketer Mark Waugh own the win as the 'biggest upset I can remember in Australia', while Pat Cummins admitted there was no excuse for the hosts' failure to penetrate with the ball.

The two teams will face off again in the second Test scheduled to begin in Mackay on August 22.

headline: EC validates nominations of Mirza Fakhrul and Oli Ahmed for presidential poll
summary: The Election Commission has cleared the nomination papers of both candidates after scrutiny, paving the way for the 23rd presidential election.
details: The Election Commission (EC) has declared the nomination papers of presidential candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as valid.
Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin conducted the scrutiny process at the EC building on Sunday afternoon.
The nomination was approved after no inconsistencies were found during the verification process.
Additionally, the nomination of Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, was also declared valid.
The 23rd presidential election is scheduled to take place on August 20.
Candidates have until 4:00 PM on August 18 to withdraw their candidacies.
caption:
The race for the presidency is set. The EC has cleared the nominations of Mirza Fakhrul and Oli Ahmed.

The Election Commission (EC) has declared the nomination papers of presidential candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as valid.

Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin conducted the scrutiny process at the EC building on Sunday afternoon.

The nomination was approved after no inconsistencies were found during the verification process.

Additionally, the nomination of Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, was also declared valid.

The 23rd presidential election is scheduled to take place on August 20.

Candidates have until 4:00 PM on August 18 to withdraw their candidacies.
